Sample.evidence_source: The lead investigator and author of this study is an enrolled member of the Cowichan Tribes who was born and raised in the community.

Type.evidence_source: Over the course of 16 months, she spent approximately 12 weeks immersed in intimate study and firsthand participation (Merriam, 2009) in the Cowichan community, including an 8-week stay after multiple suicides in the spring of 2014. Thus, she was able to make ethnographic observations and interpretations informed by cultural and social knowledge. As an insider, she has a deep understanding of the Cowichan ceremonies and other topics discussed by participants, so her analysis is grounded in an emic perspective. Notably, the community hosted a mask dance ceremony to honor her work and offer her spiritual support, effectively strengthening community-based relationships and enhancing trust between researcher and community members.
